newsitem.title: CHINA: China children to sue HK govt on deportation law.
newsitem.headline: China children to sue HK govt on deportation law.

text.p: Chinese children prepared on Thursday to sue the Hong Kong government over a law that will have illegal child immigrants deported back to China.
A group of mainland-born children applied for legal aid to mount a court challenge to the legality of their deportation.
Authorities said 14 children had so far sought legal aid and would hear by the weekend if their applications were successful, government radio said.
The Legal Aid Department expected more applications to follow and was setting up a special staff to handle the cases.

On Wednesday the new legislature, installed after Britain handed Hong Kong back to China last week, rubber-stamped a government bill allowing illegal child immigrants to be repatriated even if they have the right of abode here.

Hundreds, possibly thousands, of children have been smuggled into Hong Kong over the past year or so to join parents who already have residency rights. The alternative to sneaking in was a long wait for official migration clearance in China.
The heartbreak deportation law is under attack for violating the constitution and human rights.
Law professor Nihal Jayawickrama said the bill violated the Basic Law, which gives children the legal right to join parents who already are permanent residents.
"What's happening here is that the fundamental law of Hong Kong, the Basic Law, is being infringed upon right from the beginning," Jayawickrama said.

"Such an abrogation of these children's rights is particularly serious because it sets a precedent...of denying by administrative measures the constitutional rights of the Hong Kong people," the watchdog Hong Kong Human Rights Monitor said.

An estimated 66,000 mainland children are waiting to join parents in Hong Kong. The government hopes the new law will deter them from sneaking across in large numbers, and encourage them instead to go through proper formalities.
Chinese authorities further beefed up border patrols this week, reports said.
